Von Willebrand disease (vWD) is an inherited bleeding disorder that affects the blood's ability to clot. It is caused by a problem with von Willebrand factor, which is a protein that helps platelets stick together to form clots. There are three types of vWD: Type 1: The most common type, accounting for about 75% of cases. People with type 1 vWD have low levels of von Willebrand factor. Type 2: This type accounts for about 20% of cases. People with type 2 vWD have normal or high levels of von Willebrand factor, but it doesn't work properly. Type 3: This is the least common type, accounting for about 5% of cases. People with type 3 vWD have very little or no von Willebrand factor.

Crohn's disease is an inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) that can affect any part of the gastrointestinal tract from mouth to anus, but most commonly involves the terminal ileum and adjacent colon. It is characterized by transmural inflammation with formation of granulomas. The disease may be limited to the mucosa or involve the entire thickness of the bowel wall. The disease may be chronic or acute. The clinical manifestations of Crohn's disease include abdominal pain, diarrhea, fever, weight loss, and fatigue. The disease may be asymptomatic. The diagnosis of Crohn's disease is based on the presence of characteristic endoscopic findings, histologic evidence of transmural inflammation, and exclusion of other causes of similar symptoms. The treatment of Crohn's disease includes medical therapy, surgical intervention, and dietary modification. Ref: Ghai essential of pediatrics, 8th edition

Ans. B. ADHD (Ref: Nelson 20th ed., 1375)ADHD is a neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by inattention, hyperactivity and impulsivity. It is one of the most common childhood disorders and can continue through adolescence and adulthood. Symptoms usually appear before age 7 years and are present for more than 6 months. Inattention, hyperactivity and impulsivity are the three core symptoms of ADHD. Inattention includes difficulty sustaining attention in tasks or play activities, difficulty in maintaining focus on a task or play activity, easily distracted by extraneous stimuli, forgetful in daily activities, difficulty in processing information as quickly and accurately as others, daydreaming, fidgeting with hands or squirming in seat. Hyperactivity-impulsivity includes excessive running about or climbing in children, in adolescents and adults, restlessness, difficulty in remaining seated when expected to do so, difficulty in playing or engaging in leisure activities quietly, talking excessively, blurting out answers before questions have been completed, having difficulty awaiting turn in games. Diagnosis of ADHD is based on clinical assessment. A thorough history should be taken from parents and teachers. The diagnosis of ADHD requires the presence of at least 6 symptoms of inattention and/or hyperactivity-impulsivity that have been present for at least 6 months to a degree that is maladaptive and inconsistent with developmental level. The symptoms must also cause clinically significant impairment in social, academic or occupational functioning. The symptoms must not be better accounted for by another mental disorder.

Answer: B. ADHD
